open_magnetar.dense_bit_scan_note: Mosaic phase-1 region sums (om-mosaic region_sums) and the packed ring-switch partial evaluations (om-pcs partial_evals_packed) take eight rows at a time when they are dense: om-field subset::subset_sums8 builds the 256 subset sums of the eight eq values and subset::column_bytes transposes the rows so that one table lookup per column replaces up to eight additions. Sparse groups keep the per-bit path. Field addition is XOR, so the sums and the proofs are unchanged.
open_magnetar.glue_copy_note: Borrow addresses in the existing onehot packer and hash public words with identical little-endian framing without a serialized copy on little-endian targets. RingSwitch generates initial field elements from packed u64 pairs; Ligerito allocates its canonical packed table once after RingSwitch, borrows its first Eq fold and consumes it for query encoding. Existing owned/repacking APIs and paired/fused arithmetic remain. No witness table or codewords are retained across the IOP; proof/transcript values are unchanged.
open_magnetar.masked_native_domain_api_note: Expose existing Eq-factor coefficient reconstruction, batch inversion and wire-evaluation helpers for the proof-compatible native-domain masked-value driver. Existing helper arithmetic and other sumcheck kernels are unchanged.
open_magnetar.mosaic_prefix_note: Add explicit verifier-provided low-prefix linear functionals for compact Flock gate layouts. Their ordered descriptors are bound before batching; the packed phase folds small multilinear basis tables and retains the existing high-coordinate scans and ordinary final G opening. Empty functional lists delegate to the legacy APIs exactly. RingSwitch and Ligerito are unchanged.
open_magnetar.mosaic_profiling_note: mosaic.bind_g and mosaic.dense isolate full-layout work from per-component batching. Profiling is transcript-neutral.
open_magnetar.mosaic_scratch_note: Dense-row subset lookup scratch is retained per Rayon fold and allocated lazily; sparse groups allocate none. Arithmetic and transcript remain unchanged.

notes: Every warmup/measured proof independently verified; identical initial/access trace and exact final memory checked across methods. With public final memory each verifier checks the statement's final memory; with private final memory the cross-method check compares the final memories the provers computed, which the verifiers bind only through the commitment.

Schema 5: per workload, every configuration is warmed up, then measured in --repeat rounds; each round runs every configuration once and the order reverses every round. samples[].iteration is the round and samples[].position the order within it. paired_ratios gives ratios of medians with 95% paired bootstrap intervals over rounds (10,000 resamples, fixed seed).

Schema 5 also records verifier spans (profiler cleared before verify, taken after), structural proof sizes (field 16 B, hash 32 B, index 4 B; split PCS/Mosaic/IOP), composed soundness (union bound of Ligerito soundness_bits on the actual parameters and IOP terms; soundness.iop_source says whether the IOP terms come from the argument crate, a local fallback derived from the verifier, or only the fingerprint term), load averages per case and sample, host metadata, cases[].throughput (median prover ns per trace row and, for guests, per source load/store before narrow-store expansion) and metadata.reuse_distance (log2 buckets of operations since the previous access to the same word).

Operations mode preserves explicit load/store kinds and exactly T operation rows. All baselines use the same rows after replay conversion; reads write back their old word and writes acquire an internal old-value read. It does not infer kinds from equal values. Operation flags and values are included in operation_trace_sha256.

Inclusive commit/open and Mosaic totals are reconstructed from the exclusive span partition; IOP+prep includes preparation, argument and unattributed time. Derived actual/estimated sample totals are medianed independently.

Padding-adjusted values model commitment padding only: each commitment domain multiplies its measured commit time by its own populated/padded fraction; the estimated prover total subtracts only that modeled commitment saving. These are linear cost estimates, not measured unpadded proofs or achievable speedups. Fixed overhead and domain-size-dependent logarithmic commitment work are approximated. Opening, Mosaic, ordering, other RAM IOP, packing, public boundaries, verification and unattributed time remain fully charged. Actual padded timings and all exclusive stages are preserved.

Spice commits access/final predecessors and ripple carries. Typed Spice commits one value, is-write and next-is-write flags, with an additional initial next-is-write bitplane; mask reduction and actual component/Mosaic padding costs are included. Initial memory is public and transcript-bound. Final memory is public and transcript-bound unless cases[].final_memory is private, in which case it is committed and bound by a Mosaic claim.
cases[].implementation names the prover a method name ran. In this binary twist is Twist v2 (ram_argument::twist2); binaries before schema 5 used twist for the prover now called twist-legacy.

twist-logup-star retains the Twist v2 read check, commits dense Boolean address planes and Inc, uses a cubic cycle check, and authenticates its sparse-address evaluation directly as a LogUp* pushforward MLE. The auxiliary field table is committed before the rational challenge; both main and auxiliary Mosaic/PCS openings are charged. No public-table inner-product or dualization is run. area.commitments lists each actual domain; aggregate committed_bits need not be a power of two. The rational error is (2^address_bits-1)/2^128 with rangechecked addresses, independent of access count; full composition adds the other IOP terms and both PCS domains. Equal overall security is not claimed.

Current GP field is GF128. Its (T+N)/2^128 term and other errors prevent inferring equal/composed 120-bit security from the inherited PCS profile. Larger-field GP requires a separately authenticated extension opening adapter.
